newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: KAL considers 24 hr Seoul cargo operatio.
newsitem.headline: KAL considers 24 hr Seoul cargo operatio.

text.p: Korean Air Lines (KAL) ) is considering opening its dedicated cargo centre at Seoul's Kimpo airport round the clock and this is expected to increase throughput by 50 percent, Jong Joo Lee, KAL's airport cargo traffic office vice president, said.
Until now the flag carrier's 600,000 tonnes per year capacity terminal has been closed between midnight to 0600 local time (1500 to 2100gmt).
Lee told Reuters in an interview that the initiative will help make Kimpo more competitive when trying to win business from rival airports.
"It should also help Korean Air grow as a cargo airline," he added.

"We do not know for definite whether we will definitely go ahead but we hope to change into a 24 hour operation because of the benefits. It will increase cargo handling capacity by a large amount," Lee said.
Another benefit will be that trucks will avoid the capital's traffic jams by delivering cargo throughout the night while easing day time congestion.
Lee also said KAL was trying to improve efficiency at the cargo centre -- built in 1988 -- and which now exceeds its design capacity.
Improved operating and computer systems together with personnel training were all aimed at handling cargo more efficiently until KAL's new cargo hub opens at Inchon airport, Lee added
Seoul's new man-made Inchon island airport now under construction includes three cargo terminals and the largest costing $100 with 1.6 million tonnes annual capacity will belong to KAL.
KAL officials said Inchon is expected to open in 2001. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
